primary_diagnosis: Resistant hypertension – secondary cause not yet excluded
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient is a 48‑year‑old male with stage 2 hypertension uncontrolled on an ACE‑inhibitor, borderline renal dysfunction, and an A1c of 6.8 % that meets criteria for diabetes. The combination of uncontrolled BP, dyslipidaemia, and hyperglycaemia fulfills metabolic‑syndrome criteria and raises the likelihood of early CKD. Data gaps (potassium/renin/aldosterone, urine albumin, BMI, iron studies, thyroid panel, sleep study) prevent definitive attribution of the hypertension to a primary versus secondary cause, but the resistant nature of the hypertension makes secondary hypertension the most probable root cause. Anxiety and possible obstructive sleep apnea are important modifiers that can exacerbate BP and metabolic disturbances. Mild anemia with leukopenia and elevated PDW remains unexplained pending iron and marrow work‑up.
